interface.signature: def isCircle(N: int, A: list[str]) -> int:

preconditions.description: The input size N must be between 1 and 10^4 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(s) <= 20 for s in A)
preconditions.description: Each string in A must have a length between 1 and 20 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in A)
preconditions.description: All strings in A must consist of lowercase alphabetic characters only.
The length of A must exactly match the given N.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if and only if (all(len(edges) == 2 for edges in degree.values()) and len(edges) == N and any(edges for edges in degree.values()))
postconditions.description: The function returns 1 if and only if the strings can form a circle, meaning the graph of first/last characters forms an Eulerian circuit (all nodes have even degree and the graph is connected). Here, `degree` is a dictionary where keys are characters and values are the count of edges (connections) for that character, computed as follows: for each string s in A, increment degree[s[0]] and degree[s[-1]] by 1.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 0 if and only if not (all(len(edges) == 2 for edges in degree.values()) and len(edges) == N and any(edges for edges in degree.values()))
postconditions.description: The function returns 0 if the strings cannot form a circle, meaning the graph of first/last characters does not form an Eulerian circuit (e.g., some node has odd degree, or the graph is disconnected).
